answer: A useful Sybil defense is to require each agent to escrow a scarce, slashable stake before it can influence a market’s reputation or vote. The protocol caps each stake’s weight and penalizes agents whose attestations are contradicted by later outcomes, so splitting one identity into many does not multiply influence for free. An attacker must lock real capital across the horizon of the test and risk losing it; the karst may hide many identities, but the ridge of collateral makes mass fabrication costly.
